title: First Token Matters: Understanding Safety Collapse in Large Reasoning Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.18471v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) exhibit strong problem-solving abilities, yet their safety alignment often degrades when handling harmful queries. Existing approaches to improving safety largely rely on additional training or preference optimization, while offering limited understanding of the internal mechanisms behind safety failures. In this work, we investigate this failure through a token-level positional analysis of refusal dynamics and identify a localized vulnerability at the onset of reasoning, which we term Onset Refusal Collapse (ORC). We find that the refusal-related signal of LRMs drops sharply at the first generated token under harmful queries, which is associated with unsafe response generation. Motivated by this finding, we propose SafeToken, a lightweight inference-time intervention that injects a learned continuous safety anchor precisely at reasoning onset. translated_title: 首词元至关重要：理解大型推理模型中的安全性崩塌
translated_abstract: 大型推理模型（LRMs）展现出强大的问题解决能力，然而在处理有害查询时，其安全对齐往往会退化。现有提升安全性的方法主要依赖额外的训练或偏好优化，而对安全失效背后的内部机制理解有限。在这项工作中，我们通过对拒绝动态进行词元级位置分析来研究这种失效现象，并识别出推理起始阶段存在的一种局部脆弱性，我们将其命名为“起始拒绝崩塌”。我们发现，在有害查询下，大型推理模型与拒绝相关的信号在生成的第一个词元处急剧下降，这与不安全响应的生成密切相关。基于这一发现，我们提出了SafeToken，这是一种轻量级的推理时干预方法，它在推理起始阶段精确注入一个学习到的连续安全锚点。尽管仅更新单个词元嵌入，SafeToken的效果……
tldr: 该研究发现了大型推理模型在处理有害查询时首个生成词元的拒绝信号会急剧下降的“起始拒绝崩塌”现象，并提出仅通过在推理起始处注入单个学习到的安全锚点词元嵌入的轻量级干预方法SafeToken，即可有效恢复模型安全性。
en_tdlr: This work identifies Onset Refusal Collapse (ORC) in large reasoning models, where refusal signals drop sharply at the first generated token under harmful queries, and proposes SafeToken, a lightweight inference-time intervention that restores safety by injecting a learned continuous safety anchor precisely at reasoning onset.
